questions.q: A person who is legally recognized as a full member of a state, possessing rights and corresponding responsibilities, is known as a...
questions.explain: A **citizen** is a legal member of a sovereign political community who owes allegiance to the state and is entitled to full civil, political, and social rights, as well as the protection of the government.

questions.q: According to the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, a foreign woman who is married to a Nigerian citizen can acquire Nigerian citizenship through...
questions.explain: Under Chapter III of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution, citizenship can be acquired by **birth**, **registration**, or **naturalization**. A foreign woman married to a Nigerian citizen is entitled to acquire citizenship by *registration* upon fulfilling statutory conditions.

questions.q: The primary objective of **citizenship education** in a democratic nation is to...
options: prepare citizens for compulsory armed combat.
instill democratic values and civic responsibilities in individuals.
encourage citizens to boycott national elections.
train individuals exclusively for partisan political leadership.
questions.explain: **Citizenship education** aims to enlighten individuals about their rights, duties, obligations, and democratic principles to help them become active, responsible, and informed contributors to national development.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental goal of citizenship education in secondary schools?
options: Promoting ethnic loyalty above national interest
Eliminating the need for law enforcement agencies
Creating awareness of fundamental human rights and obligations
Restricting civic participation to civil servants
questions.explain: A major goal of citizenship education is to create awareness among youth about their **fundamental human rights**, the rule of law, and their civic responsibilities toward nation-building.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a **civic obligation** of a citizen?
options: Prompt payment of lawful taxes and rates
questions.explain: Civic duties and obligations are mandatory responsibilities imposed on citizens by law. The prompt and regular **payment of taxes and rates** is a primary civic duty required to fund public infrastructure and state operations.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: While exercising the right to freedom of expression, a responsible citizen is legally bound to avoid...
options: criticizing the economic policies of the government.
defaming the character and reputation of another individual.
publishing analytical articles in national dailies.
joining a registered opposition political party.
questions.explain: Every right comes with corresponding responsibilities and legal limits. The right to freedom of expression does not protect **slander or libel** (defamation), hate speech, or incitement to violence.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct

questions.q: The strong feeling of devotion, love, and loyalty shown by an individual towards their country is termed...
questions.explain: **Nationalism** is the sense of national consciousness and loyalty exalting one nation above all others, characterized by deep patriotism and dedication to the sovereignty and progress of one's country.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct

questions.q: Which of the following historical figures is widely celebrated as one of the founding pioneers of Nigerian nationalism?
questions.explain: **Herbert Macaulay** is widely regarded as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism.' He founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) in 1923 and vehemently opposed colonial injustices, unlike the colonial governors listed in the other options.

questions.q: National consciousness and unity in Nigeria are actively promoted by the government through the...
options: establishment of ethnically segregated public schools.
prioritization of regional customs over the federal constitution.
questions.explain: The **National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)** was established in 1973 specifically to foster national integration, inter-ethnic harmony, and national consciousness among Nigerian graduates.

questions.q: On the Nigerian Coat of Arms, the **two white horses** represent...
questions.explain:
The symbols on the Nigerian Coat of Arms carry specific meanings:

| Symbol | Representation |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Black Shield** | Fertile agricultural soil of Nigeria |
| **Two White Horses** | Dignity and pride |
| **Red Eagle** | Strength |
| **'Y' Shape (Silver Pall)** | Confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue |
| **Costus Spectabilis (Flower)** | National beauty |

questions.q: An organized group of citizens that influences government policies to protect public welfare without contesting for political office functions as a...
questions.explain: A **pressure group** is an association of individuals with common interests who seek to influence government policies, legislation, and public opinion without attempting to capture political power directly.

questions.q: Which of the following actions best illustrates a youth demonstrating nationalistic behaviour?
options: Disrupting electoral processes during national polls
Participating actively in community self-help development projects
Refusing to pay statutory local government rates
Prioritizing ethnic interests above national security
questions.explain: Nationalistic behaviour involves selflessness and positive contributions toward community and national development, such as volunteering in **community self-help projects**.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major **local civic problem** hindering community progress in Nigeria?
questions.explain: **Cultism and youth restiveness** are prominent local civic problems that disrupt peace, threaten security, destroy property, and deter economic development in Nigerian communities.

questions.q: Which of the following issues is categorized as a **global civic problem** requiring international collaboration?
options: Boundary demarcation between two local government wards
Global climate change and environmental degradation
Collection of local market stall levies
Appointment of a traditional community head
questions.explain: Global civic problems are transnational challenges that exceed the boundary of any single country and require international cooperation. **Climate change**, terrorism, and international human trafficking are prime examples.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following approaches is **NOT** a constructive method for solving civic problems in a nation?
options: Conducting public awareness campaigns through the National Orientation Agency (NOA)
Consistent and impartial enforcement of the law
Providing technical skills acquisition programs for youths
Suppressing freedom of speech and citizen feedback
questions.explain: Suppressing free speech and public feedback alienates citizens and weakens governance. Sustainable solutions to civic problems require public enlightenment, rule of law, economic empowerment, and open dialogue.
